caption:
How much tax to set aside from every invoice, by yearly profit (sole traders, 2026–27).

$75,000 profit → about 20% (roughly $14,520 in tax and Medicare)
$100,000 → about 23% ($22,520)
$125,000 → about 25% ($30,520)
$150,000 → about 27% ($39,570)
$200,000 → about 30% ($59,870)

That's income tax at 2026–27 resident rates plus the 2% Medicare levy, worked out on profit (income minus expenses) and rounded up a little. The small business tax offset can take up to $1,000 off.

Two things it doesn't include:
- GST. If you're registered, the GST you collect was never yours. Park it separately.
- Other income. A salary on top pushes the ABN income into higher brackets.

Nobody withholds tax for a sole trader, so the set-aside is the plan.

Do you move tax into a separate account?

#soletrader #smallbusinessaustralia #taxplanning #keepmore #abn
figures_checked: Resident rates 2026–27: nil to $18,200; 15c to $45,000; $4,020 + 30c to $135,000; $31,020 + 37c to $190,000; $51,370 + 45c above; Medicare levy 2% not included (ATO Tax rates – Australian residents, checked 15 Nov 2026)

Small business income tax offset: 16% of tax on net small business income, capped at $1,000, aggregated turnover under $5 million, sole traders and partners only, 2026–27 (ATO Small business income tax offset, checked 15 Nov 2026)
